newsitem.title: UK: Chinese 1997 copper ore imports to hit one mln tns.
newsitem.headline: Chinese 1997 copper ore imports to hit one mln tns.

text.p: China has become a major force in copper concentrates in recent years, and its 1997 import requirement is set to exceed one million tonnes for the first time ever, industry specialists Brook Hunt and Associates said.

"During 1996, China is believed to have imported nearly 800,000 tonnes of gross weight concentrate (220,000 tonnes contained copper), a rise of 65 percent over receipts in 1995," it said in a special report.

With an additional 200,000 tonnes of concentrates expected to be purchased this year to feed the new Jinlong smelter/refinery complex, China will become the world's second largest buyer of custom concentrate after Japan and ahead of Germany, it said.
Compared with 1995, Chinese copper smelter production is seen doubling by 2000, mainly due to incremental expansions.

Meanwhile, some 10 million tonnes of ore mining capacity will be lost, due to reserve depletion. But mine expansions at existing operations and the commissioning of a few medium-sized mines will result in a modest overall rise in mine output.

"Because of this, China's concentrate import requirement is expected to rise at an average rate of 30 percent a year between 1996 and 2000 to reach 2.2 million tonnes (625,000 tonnes of contained copper)," Brook Hunt said.
